newsitem.title: JAPAN: ALPINE SKIING-FURUSETH LEADS WORLD CUP SLALOM.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-FURUSETH LEADS WORLD CUP SLALOM.

text.p: Norways Ole Christian Furuseth was leading after the first leg of a men's World Cup slalom on Sunday which more than a third of the starters failed to finish.

Furuseth negotiated the 607-metre Mount Yakebitai course in driving snow in 48.93 seconds. Thomas Stangassinger of Austria finished .39 seconds behind, while Norwegian Tom Stiansen was a further three-hundredths of a second back.

Among the non-finishers was World Cup slalom leader Thomas Sykora of Austria, Italian ski ace Alberta Tomba and Swiss Michael von Gruenigen, who clinched the giant slalom title with a win on nearby Mount Higashidate on Saturday.
Tomba, fourth-ranked in the slalom standings, said he was still fighting jetlag.
"It is too early in the morning for me," he said. "Im sorry for the people who came to watch me."
Norwegian Kjetil Andre Aamodt, who is chasing Luc Alphand for the World Cup overall lead, was 12th.
